_meta.description: US-code dimensional limits per asset_type. Hard min/max plus defaults, each with a source citation. Values are authored in the unit given per rule; the validator converts as needed.
_meta.disclaimer: Design-reference values compiled from public standards (AASHTO, MUTCD, ADA, IBC) and typical DOT drawings. Verify against the governing local code before construction use.

code_authorities.ADA: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Standards for Accessible Design, 2010 — federal civil-rights law setting minimum accessibility requirements for the built environment.
code_authorities.AIA: American Institute of Architects — professional architectural body publishing design guidelines and graphic standards; not itself a numbered dimensional code, so it is never cited as a code_ref here.
code_authorities.IBC: International Building Code, published by the International Code Council (ICC) — the model building code most US jurisdictions adopt (often with local amendments).
code_authorities.ANSI_A117.1: ICC/ANSI A117.1 Standard for Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities — the technical accessibility standard IBC incorporates by reference; largely harmonized with the ADA Standards.
code_authorities.AASHTO: American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials — publishes roadway, lighting, and structural design guides (e.g. the Roadway Lighting Design Guide, LTS-6) used for street furniture and signage structures.
code_authorities.MUTCD: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) — governs signs, signals, and markings on public roads.
code_authorities.PROWAG: Public Right-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines, US Access Board — accessibility guidance for sidewalks, curb ramps, and other public right-of-way elements (pending full ADA rule adoption but widely applied as best practice).
code_authorities.AWWA: American Water Works Association — publishes water-utility manuals (e.g. M17) covering fire hydrant design and installation practice.

_connections.note: Heuristic fabrication reference for generated connection hardware — fastener classes, torque values, and anchor tiers the generator sizes against. NOT engineering design: a licensed engineer must verify structural connections and anchorage.

set_screw_torque_nm.note: Slip-fitter set screws (grade 45H cup point bearing on a pole tenon), sized to the fit and snapped to the bolt catalog names. Heuristic pole-fitter convention, not the bolted-joint torque table.

edge_distance.rule: 1.5d minimum from bolt center to member edge

street_light.source: AASHTO Roadway Lighting Design Guide; local DOT typical drawings

pole_height.note: Roadway lighting pole height; 25-35 ft typical for arterials.

arm_length.note: Mast arm length from pole face to luminaire.

luminaire_mount_height.note: Luminaire must clear a walkway by at least 8 ft.

ratios.note: Tapered steel light poles run a base:top diameter ratio of roughly 1.6-2.2 (deflection-driven proportion, not FEA).

pedestrian_lamp.source: AASHTO Roadway Lighting Design Guide; municipal streetscape standards

mount_height.note: Bottom of sign at least 7 ft above the sidewalk in pedestrian areas.

bollard.source: ADA/PROWAG detectability guidance; typical site-furnishing specs

height.note: 30-36 in tall so it is cane-detectable and visible.

bench.source: ADA Accessibility Standards 903.3, 903.4, 903.5; typical site-furnishing specs

seat_height.note: Accessible bench seat height 17-19 in above ground.

seat_length.note: Accessible bench seat is at least 42 in long.

back_height.note: Where provided, back support extends at least 18 in above the seat surface.

height.note: Handrail height measured above stair nosing / walking surface.

grip_diameter.note: Circular gripping surface diameter for accessible handrails, 1.25-2 in.

wall_clearance.note: Minimum clearance between the handrail gripping surface and an adjacent wall.

clear_height.note: Minimum clear opening height for door props.

clear_width.note: Minimum clear opening width, measured door face to stop with the door open 90 degrees. A 36 in nominal leaf typically yields the 32 in clear opening.

threshold_height.note: Maximum threshold height at accessible doorways is 1/2 in (beveled above 1/4 in); 0 in (flush) is always compliant.

fire_hydrant.source: AWWA M17; typical municipal water standards

outlet_height.note: Lowest outlet at least 18 in above finished grade.

drinking_fountain.source: ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 2010 — Section 602 Drinking Fountains and Water Coolers; Section 306 Knee and Toe Clearance

spout_height.note: Spout outlet 36 in maximum above the floor or ground for a wheelchair-accessible (forward-approach, knee-clearance) unit.

knee_clearance_height.note: 602.2 requires knee and toe clearance per Section 306; 306.3.1 defines the knee-clearance zone as the space 9-27 in above the floor, so the unit's underside must clear at least 27 in.

spout_reach.note: Spout located 5 in maximum from the front edge of the unit (including bumpers), and 15 in minimum from the vertical support, so a forward-approach wheelchair user can reach it.

ramp.source: ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 2010 — Section 405 Ramps

clear_width.note: Clear width of a ramp run (and between handrails, where provided) is 36 in minimum.

max_rise_per_run.note: Rise for any single ramp run is 30 in maximum. A ramp's running slope is separately capped at 1:12 (ADA-405.2) — a ratio of rise to horizontal run length, not a length itself, so it is not modeled as a parameter or sizing ratio here (this entry has no run-length parameter to form a real of/to pair against).

landing_length.note: Landing clear length is 60 in minimum.

accessible_table.source: ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 2010 — Section 902 Dining Surfaces and Work Surfaces; Section 306 Knee and Toe Clearance

surface_height.note: Tops of dining/work surfaces are 28-34 in above the floor or ground.

knee_clearance_height.note: 902.2 requires knee and toe clearance per Section 306; 306.3.1 defines the knee-clearance zone as the space 9-27 in above the floor, so the underside must clear at least 27 in.

toe_clearance_depth.note: Where toe clearance is required as part of the clear floor space, it must extend 17 in minimum under the element.

trash_receptacle.source: ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 2010 — Section 308 Reach Ranges

operable_part_height.note: Operable parts (e.g. a lid or door) must fall within the unobstructed forward/side reach range: 15 in minimum to 48 in maximum above the floor or ground.
